cap: Follicular cells and C cells reach the thyroid by different routes. Follicular cells are pharyngeal-floor endoderm that descends from the foramen cecum along the thyroglossal duct, which explains the midline position of a thyroglossal duct cyst, a pyramidal lobe and a lingual thyroid. C cells are neural crest that arrives through the fourth pouch.
teach: Match each remnant to where descent stopped: at the start (lingual thyroid), along the way (thyroglossal duct cyst) or at the end (pyramidal lobe). Because C cells arrive separately from neural crest, a calcitonin-secreting medullary carcinoma has a different cell of origin from papillary or follicular carcinoma.
